title: Smooth connected derived subgroups and commutators on rational points
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $H$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type. The smallest closed subgroup $D_H\subset H$ through which the commutator morphism $(x,y)\mapsto xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ factors exists, is normal, smooth, connected, affine and of finite type. Its rational points satisfy $D_H(F)=[H(F),H(F)]$, where the right side is the abstract subgroup generated by the commutators. Every group-scheme homomorphism $H\to C$ to a commutative affine $F$-group scheme is trivial on $D_H$.

proof.text: Write $c(x,y)=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ and $w_n:H^{2n}\to H$ for the product of $n$ such commutators. This is a morphism, takes the identity tuple to $e$, and satisfies $c(x,y)^{-1}=c(y,x)$ over every $F$-algebra. Apply [lem-sfb-pointed-word-kernel-stabilization] with $G=J=H$, $r=2$, $\varphi=c$. It gives geometric integrality of every power of $H$, kernels $I_n=\ker(w_n^*)$ eventually equal to the prime ideal $I_N$, and $I:=\bigcap_{n\geq1}I_n=I_N$. In particular $X=H^2$ is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected.

source.place: Proposition 6.20(a), p.130, with the commutator maps (37)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup] to $X=H^2$, $o=(e,e)$ and $\varphi=c$. Inversion stability was checked in step 1, so $D=\operatorname{Spec}(F[H]/I)$ is the smallest closed subgroup through which $c$ factors, affine and of finite type. It is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected because $X$ has those properties. By [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] it is smooth. Moreover $I=I_N$ is prime, so $D$ is integral and the factorization $v_N:H^{2N}\to D$ of $w_N$ has dense image and injective pullback, by [lem-sfb-pointed-word-kernel-stabilization].

source.place: Propositions 2.46, 2.48 and 6.18, Corollary 6.19(b), pp.54–55,129; Proposition 6.20(a), p.130

proof.text: Both source and target of $v_N$ are affine schemes of finite type over $F$. Apply both clauses of [lem-wf-affine-constructible-open] to its dense image. There is a nonempty open $U\subseteq D$ contained in that image. Every $u\in U(F)$ lifts to an $F$-point of $H^{2N}$: its fibre is a nonempty affine finite-type $F$-scheme, whose nonzero coordinate ring has a maximal ideal; [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing](1) makes the corresponding closed point $F$-rational. Thus $U(F)\subseteq w_N(H(F)^{2N})$. The same closed-point argument, applied to a nonempty principal open inside any nonempty open of $D$, shows that every such open has an $F$-point.

source.place: Proposition 6.20(b), p.130, constructible image and its open subset

proof.text: Let $K\subseteq H(F)$ be the abstract subgroup generated by commutators. Since $c$ factors through the closed subgroup $D$, $K\subseteq D(F)$. For $d\in D(F)$, the opens $U$ and $dU$ intersect: $D$ is irreducible, and translation by $d$ is an isomorphism with inverse translation by $d^{-1}$. Choose $u\in (U\cap dU)(F)$ by the closed-point argument of step 3. Write $u=dv$ with $v\in U(F)$. Both $u$ and $v$ are products of $N$ commutators, so $d=uv^{-1}\in K$. This proves $D(F)=K$. Conjugation by $h\in H(F)$ preserves $K$, since $h c(x,y)h^{-1}=c(hxh^{-1},hyh^{-1})$.

source.place: Proposition 6.20(b), p.130, the open-set product argument

proof.text: To obtain normality as a group scheme, consider $q:H\times_F D\to H$, $q(h,d)=hdh^{-1}$. On $F$-points its values belong to $D(F)$ by step 4. The source is a reduced affine scheme of finite type: $H$ and $D$ are reduced, and [lem-wf-affine-product-reduced] applies. By [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing](3), $q$ factors through the closed subvariety $D$. This factorization is a scheme morphism and therefore gives $h d h^{-1}\in D(R)$ for every $F$-algebra $R$, every $h\in H(R)$ and every $d\in D(R)$. Replacing $h$ by $h^{-1}$ gives the reverse inclusion, proving normality in the sense of [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup].

source.place: Proposition 6.18 and Corollary 6.19(e), pp.129–130; normality promoted from points by the vanishing principle

proof.text: Let $f:H\to C$ be a group-scheme homomorphism to a commutative affine $F$-group scheme. For every algebra, $f(c(x,y))=f(x)f(y)f(x)^{-1}f(y)^{-1}=e_C$, so $f\circ w_N$ is the identity-valued morphism. Let $j:D\hookrightarrow H$. For any $a\in F[C]$, the difference between $(f\circ j)^*(a)$ and the pullback of $a$ by the identity-valued map $D\to C$ becomes zero under $v_N^*:F[D]\to F[H^{2N}]$. This map is injective by step 2 and [lem-sfb-pointed-word-kernel-stabilization]. Hence the difference is zero. Affine morphisms are determined by their coordinate homomorphisms [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so $f\circ j$ is the identity-valued morphism. This proves the last assertion without a finite-type or reducedness assumption on $C$.

source.place: Corollary 6.19(d), p.129, with affine coordinate-ring verification

proof_origin.place: Propositions 2.46,2.48,6.18,6.20 and Corollary 6.19; pp.54–55,129–130; explicit affine density arguments for normality and the final universal property

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q130-0d46d655b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, both new nodes and every cited statement, and checked them against Milne iAG2017 pp.54-56 (2.46-2.50) and pp.129-130 (6.16-6.22, plus the 6.19 erratum). New node lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup is Milne 2.46 with 2.48 and is true. I checked the comultiplication step via A/I tensor A/I injecting into the product over n, minimality via I(K) contained in every I_n, and the geometric properties via idempotents and nilpotents detected in A/I_n and base change (2.47). New node lem-sfb-pointed-word-kernel-stabilization is Milne 6.20(a) generalized to an arbitrary pointed map G^r to J, and is true. The powers G^m are geometrically integral, I_{n+1} is contained in I_n, the descending chain of primes stops because ht(I_1) is finite, and the injective coordinate map gives dense image. I tested both nodes on small cases: a constant map, the identity, a trivial or commutative H, and GL_n. Neither node is a duplicate: rg -L over the DAG for commutator, derived subgroup and generated-subgroup terms, and for Milne 2.46-6.20 citations, finds only citers of this item or unrelated monodromy nodes. Neither is a clause of the item. Steps: (1) c(x,y)^{-1}=c(y,x); node 2 applies with G=J=H, r=2. (2) The two nodes' I_n coincide; smoothness follows from lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth (locally of finite type and geometrically reduced). (3) Chevalley (1),(2) gives an open U inside the dense image; F-points lift via Nullstellensatz(1) on the fibre and on principal opens. (4) This step is genuinely elementary: U meets dU, so d=uv^{-1} lies in K. (5) The source of q is reduced by lem-wf-affine-product-reduced; Nullstellensatz(3) factors q through D, which gives normality on every R. (6) v_N^* is injective, so f restricted to D is trivial with no assumption on C. No hypothesis was added and no target was weakened. Accepted tool_uses: lem-wf-affine-constructible-open and lem-wf-affine-product-reduced, both generic sk-i-geometry tools that steps 3 and 5 need. No SGA citation; this is not a re-split (no repair note). No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_smooth_connected_derived_subgroup {F : Type u} [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (H : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) [Smooth H.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace H.X.left] [IsAffine H.X.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType H.X.hom] [QuasiCompact H.X.hom] : ∃ (D : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (i : D ⟶ H), IsDerivedGroupScheme i.hom.hom ∧ IsNormalSubgroupScheme i.hom.hom ∧ Smooth D.X.hom ∧ ConnectedSpace D.X.left ∧ IsAffine D.X.left ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType D.X.hom ∧ QuasiCompact D.X.hom ∧ (IsMonHom.monoidHom i.hom.hom (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of F))))).range = commutator (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of F))) ⟶ H.X) ∧ (∀ (C : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) [IsCommMonObj C.X] [IsAffine C.X.left] (f : H ⟶ C), i.hom.hom ≫ f.hom.hom = 1)
